serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Perplexity's Enterprise platform provides agency users with access to leading frontier AI models (including OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Perplexity Sonar, and more). The platform supports research and analysis across internal agency data and public sources through an intuitive conversational interface. Built on Perplexity's exabyte-scale proprietary knowledge index, responses are grounded in verifiable sources, providing trustworthy, transparent, and reliable information to users.

Through Perplexity's Search API, developers may also access Perplexity's exabyte-scale knowledge index to provide web-grounded answers in real time. The index tracks over 300bn unique URLs and processes hundreds of millions of pages per day, providing agencies a durable foundation for real time web retrieval.

Perplexity's features include robust security and compliance measures such as SAML SSO, customizable access controls and data retention, comprehensive administrative management, audit logs, and dedicated priority support. Perplexity Enterprise minimizes the risks inherent in single-model solutions, with Perplexity's model-agnostic architecture providing greater uptime and empowering IT administrators to enable and disable specific models to enforce policy compliance.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: Perplexity's FedRAMP 20x trust center contains the certification package, continuous-monitoring results, and security-posture information.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: Visit https://fedramp20x.i.perplexity.ai, sign in with a one-time PIN sent to your email address, and submit your name, agency, and purpose.

additionalRepositories.repositoryDescription: Public product documentation and user guidance are available in the Help Center. The complete OSCAL assessment package and human-readable assessment results are available to authorized agency representatives through the Trust Center or by contacting usgov@perplexity.ai.

FedRAMP 20x continuous monitoring: the live KSI dashboard, human-readable assessment reports, and the machine-readable API for agency SIEM/GRC pipelines (docs/agency_access.md, docs/programmatic_access.md).
additionalRepositories.accessRequestInstructions: Access to this continuous monitoring dashboard and its API is granted to individual authorized agency representatives (authorizing officials, auditors, and compliance leads), not to entire domains. To request access, visit https://fedramp20x.i.perplexity.ai, sign in with a one-time PIN sent to your email address, and submit the access request with your name, agency, and purpose. Access is granted when the requester is an agency representative with an authorization or oversight need. There is no need to keep the request page open: once your request is approved, your address joins the standing allowlist and you sign in at any time with just the one-time PIN. Access is per-individual, so colleagues submit their own requests. Questions can go to fedramp@perplexity.ai. Perplexity notifies FedRAMP of any denied agency request within five business days.

submissionStatement: Perplexity identifies the Cloud Service Offering's Minimum Assessment Scope as all machine-based and non-machine-based information resources that are likely to handle federal customer data or likely to affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of that data. Resource classes are bounded by approved authorization-boundary account, region, cluster, namespace, repository, third-party tenant, and organizational-function lists.

Perplexity uses a distributed inventory model in which each resource class is tied to an upstream system of record and reconciled against an independent discovery or runtime source. The GRC evidence platform stores timestamped evidence copies and lineage; the named upstream systems remain authoritative. No single tool is designated as the authoritative inventory for all information resources.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: AWS compute, storage, database, messaging, networking, IAM, cryptographic, logging, monitoring, backup, and security resources in the authorization boundary
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: AWS provider-native resource and service APIs provide the authoritative runtime inventory for the approved account and region allowlist. Versioned Terraform state identifies resources managed through Terraform, while Terraform source establishes approved intended configuration. Provider-native discovery is reconciled against Terraform to identify live, unmanaged, or drifted resources.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: Source repositories and build or deployment configuration that build, configure, deploy, test, secure, or operate the authorized offering
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: The GitHub organization repository inventory, constrained by a GRC-approved in-scope repository list, is authoritative for repository existence and status. Repository records are reconciled to Buildkite pipelines, Shipyard service definitions, Helm manifests, Terraform roots, container builds, and deployed-image provenance so that auxiliary, archived, or externally hosted deployment sources are not omitted. GitHub rulesets, branch protections, CODEOWNERS, pull-request history, and security settings provide the associated governance evidence.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: Software dependencies, base images, container images, machine images, and deployable artifacts incorporated into the authorized offering
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: GitHub dependency-graph and committed package manifests and lockfiles provide the authoritative declared-dependency inventory for each in-scope repository. The applicable container or artifact registry and image inventory provide the authoritative inventory of published artifacts, and cloud or Kubernetes runtime metadata identifies the versions actually deployed. Packer and CI/CD records provide machine-image and build lineage. Dependabot provides vulnerability and update evidence.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: Personnel functions, workforce identities, and access paths capable of changing, operating, securing, supporting, or administratively accessing the offering
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: Rippling is authoritative for employee and contractor identity, worker type, employment status, department, manager, and lifecycle status. Okta is authoritative for active workforce identities, authentication policy, groups, and application assignments. Serval is authoritative for its cataloged access roles, requests, approvals, business justifications, and time-bounded grants. Provider-native IAM and target-application entitlement inventories are authoritative for effective access. Joiner, mover, leaver, privileged-access, and exception populations are reconciled across these sources.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: Managed workforce endpoints used by personnel who can affect the authorized offering
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: IRU, formerly Kandji, is authoritative for enrolled and managed macOS endpoints and their management and configuration posture. Microsoft Intune is authoritative for managed Windows endpoints. The combined endpoint population is reconciled against the active workforce and privileged-access populations.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: Third-party cloud services, suppliers, subprocessors, external APIs or models, and externally operated security or business systems that handle federal customer data or can materially affect the offering
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: Actual technical usage is established from architecture and data-flow documentation, Terraform, deployment manifests, application configuration, provider integrations, identity or application assignments, and provider-native administration or API records. Vanta's active vendor inventory and security-review records provide the authoritative managed vendor-risk record. These sources are reconciled to contracts, DPAs, procurement or payment records, identity integrations, production configuration, and network egress. Each applicable third party is linked to its provider, use case, data handled, connection path, owner, authorization or certification status, mitigation measures, compensating controls, and lifecycle status.

resourceClasses.resourceClass: FedRAMP evidence, certification-package, and persistent-validation resources
resourceClasses.authoritativeInventory: The ppl-ai/fedramp20x GitHub repository provides the version-controlled rule mappings, metric definitions, schemas, evidence mappings, and publication code. The controlled evidence-storage path and its object metadata provide the evidence-artifact inventory.

enterpriseFlows.name: User request
enterpriseFlows.description: A user’s request first passes through Cloudflare edge network protections before reaching the AWS production load balancer.

enterpriseFlows.name: Application processing
enterpriseFlows.description: The production load balancer uses certificates managed by AWS Certificate Manager and routes requests to the production EKS cluster, which interacts with production data stores.

enterpriseFlows.name: Data replication
enterpriseFlows.description: Production data is transferred through the data lake replication service to the centralized data lake.

enterpriseFlows.name: Sandbox processing
enterpriseFlows.description: The sandbox uses a separate load balancer, EKS cluster, and data stores, with certificates managed through AWS Certificate Manager.

enterpriseFlows.name: Administrative access
enterpriseFlows.description: Perplexity engineers obtain time-limited access through Just-in-Time Access Management, while Identity Management controls access to authorized production and sandbox resources.

enterpriseFlows.name: PII access
enterpriseFlows.description: Access to PII and the data lake is restricted through strict permissions and Just-in-Time access controls.

enterpriseFlows.name: Software changes
enterpriseFlows.description: Source code changes are maintained in version control (Github) and reviewed before deployment into the AWS environment.

apiFlows.name: Request intake
apiFlows.description: Client requests pass through middleware that enforces CORS requirements and performs logging, Datadog tracing, and request correlation.

apiFlows.name: Access control
apiFlows.description: Bearer authentication validates the request, after which the system establishes user context, applies Redis-backed rate limits, and assigns request ID and timeout controls.

apiFlows.name: Endpoint routing
apiFlows.description: Authorized requests are routed to chat completions, structured responses, or embeddings endpoints.

apiFlows.name: Model configuration
apiFlows.description: The selected endpoint resolves the applicable model configuration using internal model settings, cached configuration, or supported external providers.

apiFlows.name: Search-augmented flow
apiFlows.description: Search-augmented requests may undergo query reformulation and route through Pro Search or Fast Search before the unified API engine summarizes results and generates citations.

apiFlows.name: Direct-inference flow
apiFlows.description: Direct-inference requests use model-pool selection and a primary inference client, with a legacy or fallback client available when needed, before reaching the selected inference backend.

apiFlows.name: Inference backends
apiFlows.description: Requests may be processed by Perplexity-hosted infrastructure or external model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Fireworks.

apiFlows.name: Response delivery
apiFlows.description: Results are returned as server-sent events, JSON responses with usage information, or embedding vectors, depending on the endpoint.

apiFlows.name: Supporting data flows
apiFlows.description: ElastiCache, Amazon S3, Kinesis, and Amazon RDS support rate limiting, metadata, asynchronous storage, event processing, and billing-related functions.

apiFlows.name: Observability and configuration
apiFlows.description: Datadog receives operational telemetry, and Eppo receives experimentation data, feature configuration, or evaluation information.

mas_cso_tpr.compensating_controls: Customer PII stored in Snowflake is protected by role-based dynamic data masking applied at query time, so raw PII is not visible to warehouse users by default.
mas_cso_tpr.explanation_or_justification_for_use: Data warehouse/analytics and data movement, including the Polytomic Snowflake ↔ Salesforce workflow.
mas_cso_tpr.general_usage_and_configuration: Snowflake is a data storage and processing provider used as a cloud data warehouse and analytics platform.
mas_cso_tpr.mitigation_measures: Privileged Snowflake access is provisioned just-in-time through Serval with independent approval and time-bound expiry; analytics roles are automatically deprovisioned through the Okta group/role workflow. Annual third-party risk assessments are performed as part of the vendor risk management program.

certified.name: Snowflake
certified.useCase: Snowflake is a data storage and processing provider used as a cloud data warehouse and analytics platform. Data warehouse/analytics and data movement, including the Polytomic Snowflake ↔ Salesforce workflow.

mas_cso_tpr.compensating_controls: Data synced through Airbyte pipelines is encrypted in transit, and sync schedules and destination-side retention settings are configured on Perplexity's side to limit how long data persists within pipeline-managed storage. Any anomalous sync volume or unexpected destination writes are monitored and alerted on internally.
mas_cso_tpr.explanation_or_justification_for_use: Data movement/CDC to the analytics warehouse; migrating the Stripe integration from Fivetran to Airbyte was considered as a cost-reduction option.
mas_cso_tpr.general_usage_and_configuration: Airbyte is a data ingestion platform used for data integration and movement.
mas_cso_tpr.mitigation_measures: Airbyte's production database access is limited to a read-only replica: it cannot write to production data, and its pipeline load is isolated from the production primary. Annual third-party risk assessments are performed as part of the vendor risk management program.

awsEncryption.name: Amazon RDS and Aurora
awsEncryption.description: Production databases in us-east-1 have storage encryption enabled. RDS uses AES-256 encryption with AWS KMS for database storage, logs, backups, replicas, and snapshots.

awsEncryption.name: Amazon EBS
awsEncryption.description: EBS encryption by default is enabled in us-east-1. EBS volumes use AES-256 encryption, with AWS KMS used to manage the associated encryption keys.

awsEncryption.name: Amazon S3
awsEncryption.description: Terraform-managed restricted and confidential buckets in us-east-1 have default encryption configured. Perplexity's shared modules support SSE-S3 with AES-256-GCM and SSE-KMS with envelope encryption.

awsEncryption.name: Amazon DynamoDB
awsEncryption.description: Terraform-managed restricted and confidential tables in us-east-1 are encrypted at rest with AES-256. The current tables use DynamoDB's default AWS-owned encryption keys rather than customer-managed KMS keys.

awsEncryption.name: AWS Secrets Manager
awsEncryption.description: Production application secrets are centrally stored in AWS Secrets Manager. Each secret version is protected with a 256-bit AES data key and AWS KMS envelope encryption.

awsEncryption.name: AWS KMS
awsEncryption.description: Perplexity uses symmetric AWS KMS keys for encryption key management. DataEngine uses KMS GenerateDataKey with AES_256, and SSE-KMS workloads use KMS-managed keys for envelope encryption.

awsEncryption.name: AWS Certificate Manager and load balancers
awsEncryption.description: ACM certificates are attached to production HTTPS load balancers. The configured listeners support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 for encrypted connections between Cloudflare and AWS-hosted services.

cloudflareEncryption.name: Public endpoint encryption
cloudflareEncryption.description: Cloudflare provides TLS encryption for perplexity.ai, www.perplexity.ai, and api.perplexity.ai. The endpoints use TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and support TLS 1.2 fallback with ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256.

cloudflareEncryption.name: Edge certificates
cloudflareEncryption.description: Cloudflare Universal SSL manages the public certificates used by the Perplexity endpoints.

cloudflareEncryption.name: Origin encryption
cloudflareEncryption.description: Cloudflare Full mode encrypts traffic between Cloudflare and the AWS origin. Always Use HTTPS is enabled for the active perplexity.ai zone.

applicationEncryption.name: DataEngine field encryption
applicationEncryption.description: DataEngine encrypts selected database fields with AES-256-GCM.

applicationEncryption.name: DataEngine key management
applicationEncryption.description: DataEngine uses AWS KMS to generate AES-256 branch keys.

applicationEncryption.name: Encrypted session tokens
applicationEncryption.description: Perplexity and NextAuth session tokens use direct-encryption JWE with A256GCM. NextAuth uses HKDF for key derivation and supports current and previous secrets for rotation.

applicationEncryption.name: Application identity tokens
applicationEncryption.description: Computer application identity tokens use EdDSA with Ed25519 keys and JWKS for signing and verification.

integrityProtection.name: Source-code signatures
integrityProtection.description: Production source commits use GitHub-generated PGP signatures. Protected pull requests, linear history, and squash-only merges support signature coverage on the main branch.

integrityProtection.name: Deployment artifacts
integrityProtection.description: Container manifests, container layers, Cloudflare Worker bundles, and asset manifests use SHA-256 hashes to verify content integrity.
